Morph and far-side wraps

Agent C15, 2026-10-24. Pocket fixture ux_2d_pocket.toml, tool-centre space (the pocket inset by R, the island grown by R). Python prototypes with exact geometry; no Rust, no lattice. Scripts: phase2/c15/; every number on this page is checked by assert_c15.py.

Each picture shows the same frame. The black outline is the pocket wall and the grey disc is the island. The dashed circle is the island grown by the tool radius: the cutter centre cannot go inside it. The yellow area is the zone: the area that the island hides from the entry (red dot). The green dashed lines are the two shadow lines from the entry, tangent to the grown island.

Lines: near-side wraps (circles about the entry, the same in every idea)the idea's wrapsthe harness wraps (Rust, read from the render SVG)

0. Morph fields (e), (f) and the plan (a), star and pocket

The operator saw other tools whose wraps start round and turn into the wall shape. (e) and (f) are two fields with no parameter that do this. (a) is the plan recommended for the far side, shown here on the star too. All three use the same level rule (the C5 law gap from each wrap's own curvature) and the same 0.1 mm replay. The harness renders are the v4 PNGs; the harness has no ContourParallel column (the 2D op runs contour-parallel only behind the narrow-region gate, render harness module doc).

How to read a card. "Open arcs" are wraps that do not close; each costs a plunge or a turn (problem 2). "Interior width" leaves out R of arc length at each end or seam; the ends and seams are reported apart. "Min/max gap per loop" is the smallest gap of a wrap divided by its largest gap: 1 is even.

Closed loops. Only (e) on the star keeps every wrap one closed loop (32 loops, 0 open arcs). On the pocket, (e) loops stay closed but 10 late levels are two loops, one round the island and one along the wall. (f) splits 7 star levels into up to 3 loops, and on the pocket it stops at u = 0.7857: behind the island u has a second low basin (lowest 0.7857) that the loops from the entry reach only at u = 0.8347. (a) has 56 open arcs on the star and 56 on the pocket.

Spacing and cost. (a) keeps an even gap (median min/max 0.9996 on the star). One value of u per loop gives (e) a gap that follows the field's gradient, so the loops crowd at the inner corners (narrowest gap there in 31 of 31 star loops; median 0.0243). On the star (e) needs 13 more levels and 6.1 times the cut length of (a); on the pocket 23 more levels and 8.4 times.

Load. (a) holds the ceiling in the interior on both shapes (0.3615 D star, 0.3617 D pocket; c = 0.3626 D). (e) holds it on the pocket (0.3651 D); on the star it reads 0.80 D on the last 5 loops at 4 of the five tips. (f) reads up to 0.91 D at the corners where the nearest wall changes.

Verdict. (e) removes the per-arc plunge only on a part without an island, and at 6.1 times the cut length of (a). (f) fails on load. (a) stays the recommendation; its open arcs are the C14 turns' work.

1. Why the far side wobbles

Lattice or not? geodesic_curv against the exact field

Red: the harness wraps of geodesic_curv. Blue: the exact geodesic distance at the same levels.

Look at: the red and blue lines lie on top of each other behind the island. The lattice moves a wrap by at most 0.47 mm. Along one wrap the error changes by at most 0.11 mm (standard deviation).

Seed or not? the split column against its exact field

Red: the harness zone wraps of geodesic_curv_split. Blue: the exact distance from the two shadow lines (idea C11 without the lattice).

Look at: the red wraps bend toward the wall near the top and the right. The blue wraps are straight. Along one red wrap the exact distance changes by up to 1.29 mm (standard deviation; median 0.31 mm).

Hypothesis 1 (lattice pivots): a small part. Behind the island the lattice wraps of geodesic_curv are within 0.47 mm of the exact wraps (RMS 0.18 mm; on average 0.15 mm farther out). That is less than one planner cell (0.5 mm). The visible mess behind the island in geodesic_curv comes from the spacing: the C5 law reads the front radius as R + T about the entry. Behind the island the true radius is the distance to the tangent point on the island, which is smaller. At the harness levels the exact wraps read 0.4129 D in the replay (ceiling 0.3626 D) on 172 samples, all 2.8 to 5.9 mm from the grown island. The replay refuses such steps, and each refusal leaves stock for the cuts after it: the cascade of C5.

Hypothesis 2 (jagged seed): the main cause in the split column. The zone field starts from the cleared lattice nodes, not from the shadow lines. Near the walls that set reaches into the zone, so the wraps bend toward it. The bend is 1.29 mm against 0.11 mm for the lattice alone.

Hypothesis 3 (the V at the meeting line): a corner, not a wobble. The exact split wraps (blue, right) are straight and meet in a V with a corner radius of 0.87 mm. Each V splits a wrap (8 V corners in the exact split). Ideas (c) and (d) remove it.

2. The ideas

Each idea chooses its levels by one rule: every point of a new wrap is at most the C5 law gap from the cut, with the radius read from the wrap's own curvature over one pass step (1.5 mm each side). The replay then cuts the wraps in order on a 0.1 mm grid and reads the swept width as the planner does. "Arc interior" means more than R from an arc end. The arc ends read high in every idea and on the clean near side too (near side: 0.63 D), so the ends are the wall-end class that the C14 turns address.

(a) Exact geodesic distance, curvature read locally

One front from the entry; behind the island the wraps are circle involutes. The levels use the true local radius, not R + T.

Look at: the far-side wraps continue the near-side circles without a break. They meet in a V at the top right.

The harness split column has 35 zone wraps for comparison. "(c) with the radius ρ*" uses the fillet radius ρ* = 22.74 mm that the brief suggested. That fillet is so wide that the round union no longer stays next to the cut: one wrap crosses standing stock and reads 0.99 D. The residue is a sliver at the island next to a shadow line, less than 1.5 mm from the wall; the wall pass removes it.

4. Recommendation

Next Rust step: idea (a), then (c) on top of it. Keep one field from the entry (no split). Space the levels by the C5 law with the radius read from each level's own curvature, and take the smallest allowed gap along the level. Behind the island this holds the ceiling in the replay (0.3574 D) where the harness levels did not (0.4129 D). It costs 3 levels over the whole pocket and no residue is left.

The far-side wraps of (a) are the involutes that continue the near-side circles: the clean pattern of the near side. Idea (c) then rounds the V behind the island, for 2 more levels. Idea (d) is the best split variant: one arc per level and no meeting line. Idea (b) needs more than double the cut length and is not recommended.
